rows.sentence: Based on `doc.txt` ("Money Management Tips: 55 Ways to Save Money"), here are some tips on saving money, grouped by category:
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This introduces the list and explains how it is organized.

rows.sentence: Instead of paying for a fitness club membership, buy some weights or go to the ARC.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends both alternatives to paying for a fitness club membership.

rows.sentence: Don't smoke — cigarettes are expensive, the money adds up quickly, and you'll be fined if you smoke near school facilities.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document advises against smoking and gives both the accumulating cost and the fine as reasons.

rows.sentence: Wait until after half-time at sport events and get in for free.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly recommends waiting until after halftime for free admission.

rows.sentence: When eating out, look for coupons or special deals, and order water instead of overpriced drinks.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends looking for restaurant deals and ordering water because other drinks are overpriced.

rows.sentence: Grab coupon books that local businesses give out at the beginning of the semester.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document says local businesses distribute coupon books at the start of the semester and recommends getting one.

rows.sentence: Take advantage of hundreds of free campus activities (clubs, student concerts, church-sponsored events — often with food included).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document mentions hundreds of free campus activities, recommends the three listed options, and says food is usually involved.

rows.sentence: Attend free "Illinites" student activities at the Illini Union every Friday night.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document identifies Illinites as free student activities at the Illini Union every Friday night.

rows.sentence: Attend shows at Krannert — student tickets are $10 or less, sometimes free.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends Krannert shows and gives the stated student ticket prices.

rows.sentence: If you're throwing a party, have guests pay a little or bring things to offset your cost.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document suggests both guest contributions as ways to offset the cost of a party.

rows.sentence: Don't buy a book unless you really want to keep it — you can check books out free at libraries.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document advises buying only books you want to keep and notes that libraries lend books for free.

rows.sentence: Rent movies with a group of friends, or go to second-run theaters for $1–$2 a ticket.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends both options and specifies second-run ticket prices of $1 or $2.

rows.sentence: Bring your student ID to movies — most theaters give student discounts.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends bringing a student ID and says most theaters offer student discounts.

rows.sentence: Be a savvy consumer: research product quality (e.g., through Consumer Reports) before major purchases.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends researching product quality through Consumer Reports before making a major purchase.

rows.sentence: Sometimes the cheaper product works just as well as the expensive one.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document makes the same qualified comparison.

rows.sentence: Ask for generic medications at the pharmacy.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this exact recommendation.

rows.sentence: Get your hair done at a cosmetology school instead of a salon.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends using a cosmetology school in place of a salon.

rows.sentence: Buying in bulk is usually good, but shop by per-unit price — the biggest option isn't always the best value.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document generally favors bulk buying but advises comparing unit prices because the largest option can offer worse value.

rows.sentence: Scout garage/yard sales for housewares and furniture; the YMCA holds a "dump and run" at the start of each semester.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends garage or yard sales for those items and states when the YMCA event takes place.

rows.sentence: Make things for gifts — cheaper, and the time invested shows you care.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document cites lower cost and the care shown by investing time as reasons to make gifts.

rows.sentence: Buy holiday and birthday gifts throughout the year to take advantage of sales.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly recommends this timing for gift purchases to make use of sales.

rows.sentence: Get a job at a place where you already spend a lot of money to get employee discounts.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends working where you already spend heavily so you can get employee discounts.

rows.sentence: Use mail-in rebates or coupons for groceries and health/beauty items.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends rebates or coupons for both categories of purchases.

rows.sentence: Don't buy bottled water — buy a water filtration pitcher.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends a filtration pitcher as an alternative to bottled water.

rows.sentence: Don't buy something just because it's on sale — consider whether you really need it.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document advises checking whether you need an item rather than buying it just because it is on sale.

rows.sentence: Apply for your favorite store's discount card if they have one.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends applying for a favorite store's discount card if it offers one.

rows.sentence: Make home-cooked meals — often cheaper than a fast food binge.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends home cooking to save money and gives a home-cooked dinner as often cheaper than a fast-food binge.

rows.sentence: Pack a lunch instead of eating out.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this exact recommendation.

rows.sentence: Buy clothes at the end of the season when they're on sale.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends buying clothing during end-of-season sales.

rows.sentence: Take clothes you no longer wear to a consignment shop or sell them online.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives both options for clothes you no longer wear.

rows.sentence: Share dresses and tuxes with friends for special occasions.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this exact recommendation.

rows.sentence: If you buy more than one of something (e.g., 2–3 shirts), always ask for a discount.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends asking for a discount when buying multiples and gives two or three shirts as its example.

rows.sentence: Invest in durable clothes and shoes rather than many cheap pairs.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends durable clothing and footwear over repeatedly buying cheap items.

rows.sentence: Set goals for your spending and saving.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this exact recommendation.

rows.sentence: Keep track of your spending to avoid overspending (there are apps for that).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document advises tracking spending to avoid overspending and says apps are available for this purpose.

rows.sentence: Don't use a credit card if it leads you to make more purchases — on average, people with credit cards spend 34% more.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives both the conditional warning about credit card use and the 34% average spending figure.

rows.sentence: Before going out to spend, set a limit for yourself and stick to it.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document advises setting a spending limit in advance and adhering to it.

rows.sentence: Wait at least two hours before making a big purchase to be sure it's something you really need.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document specifies both the minimum two-hour wait and its purpose.

rows.sentence: Obey traffic laws — speeding tickets cost more than the ticket itself by raising insurance premiums.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document advises obeying traffic laws and says speeding tickets increase insurance premiums in addition to costing money themselves.

rows.sentence: Keep your tires inflated properly for better gas mileage.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document links proper tire inflation to better gas mileage.

rows.sentence: Get good grades — insurance companies offer lower rates to students with a 3.0+ GPA.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends good grades as a way to qualify for favorable insurance rates and gives the same GPA threshold.

rows.sentence: Carpool with friends.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends carpooling with a friend.

rows.sentence: Search for dependable cars that offer good gas mileage.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The transportation tip recommends looking for dependability and good gas mileage; “cards” is a clear typo for “cars” in this context.

rows.sentence: Drive an older car — insurance payments and taxes will be less.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends driving an older car and gives lower insurance payments and taxes as the reasons.

rows.sentence: Walk, bike, or ride to school — good for you and saves on gas.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document lists the same alternatives and says they are good for you and save gas.

rows.sentence: Look around for the cheapest gas price before filling up (there are apps for that).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends comparing gas prices before filling up and mentions apps for doing so.

rows.sentence: Only use ATMs of your own bank — other banks' ATM fees add up.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends using only your bank's ATMs because other banks' fees accumulate.

rows.sentence: Always put part of your paycheck into a savings account.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends setting aside part of each paycheck in a savings account.

rows.sentence: Spare change adds up — use a piggy bank or change jar.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document says spare change adds up and recommends both ways of collecting it.

rows.sentence: Volunteer — if you're busy, you can't spend money (and it boosts your resume).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends volunteering to stay busy and avoid spending, and calls it a résumé booster; “month” is a clear typo for “money” in this savings tip.

rows.sentence: Use plastic grocery bags as trash can liners.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explicitly recommends this reuse of plastic grocery bags.

rows.sentence: Turn off the water while brushing your teeth.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this exact recommendation.

rows.sentence: Unplug electronics when not in use — even turned off, they still use costly energy.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends unplugging idle electronics because they still consume energy when switched off.

rows.sentence: Use items like shampoo, toothpaste, and paper towels sparingly — enough to do the job without waste.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document names the same items and recommends using only enough to avoid waste.

rows.sentence: Pay your bills online to save paper and money on stamps.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends paying bills online to save paper and avoid stamp costs.

rows.sentence: Ask your landlord to seal gaps between doors and windows to prevent heat leaks over winter.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document recommends asking the landlord to seal those gaps to prevent winter heat loss.

rows.sentence: The document notes it was modified by Joe Pleshar, Yuanhang Fan, and Maggie Benson (Peer Educators, Spring 2015) for the University of Illinois Extension Financial Wellness for College Students Program, and is sourced from the National Student Loan Program's Budget Handout #6 (2002).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document's credits identify the modifiers, their role and term, the university program, and the original handout and year.
